subject: Controller vs Processor clarity + TIA & evidence request for Order Form
messages:
From: Sylvia Park <sylvia@aureliahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Looking for clarity on controller/processor roles + TIA request

Hi Olga / Ben —

Thanks for the draft Order Form and the DPA you shared earlier. A few items popped up from our compliance and procurement teams that we need clarified before we can proceed to legal redlines:

1) Controller vs Processor: the Order Form currently refers to multiple parties as "data controllers" in different clauses. Our Data Protection Officer needs explicit confirmation of Redwood's role for the services in-scope (generation + embeddings + logging for telemetry). Please confirm whether Redwood is accepting the role of Processor and will not claim joint-controller status for the standard service offering.

2) Subprocessors & Transfer Impact: we need a current subprocessor roster and a short note on whether any subprocessors transfer data outside the EEA/UK and under what legal basis. If you have a recent Transfer Impact Assessment, please attach.

3) Technical evidence: our security team requires SOC 2 report (redacted ok), KMS key handling attestation, and a description of how you isolate customer KV cache and backups.

4) Narrowing of processing activities: the MSA currently includes broad language potentially covering model training/fine-tuning using customer data. We need to understand if Redwood might ever use customer prompts/data to fine-tune models and, if so, what opt-in/contractual controls are offered.

We attached the latest procurement checklist and the 1-page transfer questionnaire. Can we get the items above by COB Thursday 13 Aug? If to discuss, I can make time for a 30-min call.

Thanks —
Sylvia
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Aurelia Health Systems

Attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf (stub), transfer-questionnaire.xlsx (stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Looking for clarity on controller/processor roles + TIA request

Sylvia —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front and then items for Ben/Laura to pick up:

- Role: Redwood acts as a Processor for the SaaS inference service. We will not assert joint-controller status for standard inference, embeddings, or telemetry used for SLA/perf diagnostics. We can add a short clause in the Order Form confirming Processor role.

- Subprocessors: attached is our current roster (Subprocessor-Roster-2026-07.csv). High level: our stack uses cloud infra (US regions), a managed datastore for logs, and an analytics provider — all listed in roster. Some subprocessors are in the US and so transfers will occur under SCCs + appropriate TIA measures.

- Evidence: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a KMS attestation. I've attached an annotated DPA where we suggest tightening a few definitions (processing purposes + no-training clause).

- Training/fine-tuning: by default Redwood does not use customer prompts/data to train public models. Any custom fine-tuning work is on a per-engagement basis and requires explicit written opt-in and controls (we can propose language in the DPA).

Ben/Laura/Karthik — please see my annotated DPA (attached). Specific asks for legal:
  * Confirm whether the proposed "no-training without opt-in" language is sufficient.
  * Review proposed SCCs insertion points and whether we should include the EU Commission 2021 SCCs module for processor-to-processor transfers.
  * Advise on a short TIA addendum we can provide to Aurelia that summaries transfer risks and mitigations.

Sylvia — happy to do a 30-min call this Wed 11 Aug 09:30 UTC or Thu 12 Aug 14:00 UTC. Which works?

Best,
Olga
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-annotated-Redwood.pdf (annotations), Subprocessor-Roster-2026-07.csv (stub), Dataflow-Diagram.png (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alan White <awhite@barringtonlegal.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Looking for clarity on controller/processor roles + TIA request

Thanks Olga / Sylvia — I reviewed Olga's annotations and the Order Form. A few legal redline suggestions and operational commitments below (summary first, details after):

Summary (high level commitments)
- Redwood confirms Processor role for the standard service and will accept the Processor module of the SCCs.
- Redwood will not use customer data for model training or fine-tuning unless we have a separate written agreement (opt-in) that details scope, retention, and deletion commitments.
- Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II (redacted), KMS handling attestation, and the current subprocessor roster.

Redline recommendations (to be incorporated into DPA / Order Form)
1) "No-Training" clause: insert explicit prohibition against using customer content for model training absent a mutually executed SOW/addendum. Proposed phrasing attached in SCCs-redline.docx.
2) SCCs: include EU Commission 2021 SCCs and explicitly map processor-to-processor modules for any downstream subprocessors.
3) Transfer Impact Addendum: provide a 1-page TIA addendum that links to the subprocessor roster and enumerates legal bases and supplementary measures (encryption at-rest/in-transit, access controls, contractual constraints). I'll draft the addendum and share Monday EOD.
4) Narrow processing activities: revise the Order Form Appendix A to list 'inference', 'embeddings', 'telemetry for service health' only — remove ambiguous terms like 'analytics' unless defined.
5) Evidence delivery: propose the following timeline: SOC2 redacted + KMS attestation by Thu 13 Aug; TIA addendum and updated DPA redlines by Mon 17 Aug. Please confirm if that timeline is acceptable for Aurelia's procurement/legal.

Operational notes for security team (non-contractual)
- SOC 2 will be delivered under NDA redaction.
- KMS: we do not release customer CMKs; we manage keys in a shared HSM-backed KMS with per-tenant isolation for encryption at rest.
- KV cache: customer prefixes are logically separated; backups have separate retention windows per account and are encrypted.

Olga/Laura please review the attached redline docs. Sylvia if you want Alan White included on the call or to review our redlines, happy to loop him in.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SCCs-redline.docx (stub), Evidence-Delivery-Plan.xlsx (stub), draft-TIA-addendum.docx (todo)

From: Sylvia Park <sylvia@aureliahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alan White <awhite@barringtonlegal.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@procurecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Looking for clarity on controller/processor roles + TIA request

Ben/Olga —

This is helpful, thank you. Procurement and legal can work with the proposed timeline: SOC2 redacted + KMS attestation by COB Thu 13 Aug. The TIA addendum and updated DPA redlines by Mon 17 Aug are acceptable for our review cycle.

Let's take the call Thu 12 Aug 14:00 UTC (you proposed this) — Marcus (procurement) will join and Alan White will cover the legal Qs.

A couple of quick clarifying questions before the call:
- Can you confirm whether any subprocessor (listed in the roster) performs automated profiling as defined under GDPR Article 4(4)? If yes, please flag which one(s) and the purposes.
- For the "no-training without opt-in" language, our counsel will likely request a remedy/exit right if Redwood later expands service behavior. Please prepare a short exception/exit clause suggestion we can discuss.

See you on the call.

Best,
Sylvia
